title: Dispatch LTP 4: Warehouse Workers Escape as Future Report Rewrites Itself
summary: The paper warned of a locked door; the fire began at a different entrance.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: A fire broke out at the Narrow Street warehouse yesterday. All fourteen workers escaped through the side door Inspector Voss had ordered unbolted. The warehouse’s front stair filled with smoke, a detail absent from the first advance report. By evening, the early edition described the workers coming out through the side door instead.

The Chronicle has now received eight issues before their publication dates. Some of their articles have changed after the staff passed warnings to those named. Others, including notices of marriages and small trades, have remained word for word. Dr. Saye says the distinction may depend on whether anyone with knowledge of the future issue has acted.

Word of the bundles has spread beyond the pressroom. Yesterday a group assembled at our door demanding to see tomorrow’s want advertisements. One man wished to know whether his missing brother would be found. A woman asked the date of an operation her physician has not scheduled. Mr. Ashcombe refused them access.

He then discovered a new advertisement in the advance issue: “For sale: the answer to a question not yet asked.” No member of the staff has accepted payment for it. The type was set in the Chronicle’s own classified style.

Miss Celia Marsh, who examined the bundles for the Institute, noticed a faint line on the back of each page where no ordinary press impression should be. The line follows a second arrangement of type beneath the visible words. She and Dr. Saye will inspect the press after tonight’s run.
